data.name: Batman: Arkham City - Game of the Year Edition
data.detailed_description:
Batman: Arkham City aprofunda a atmosfera intensa de Batman: Arkham Asylum, levando os jogadores a sobrevoar a imensa Arkham City – cinco vezes maior do que o mundo de jogo de Batman: Arkham Asylum – o novo "lar" de segurança máxima para todos os criminosos, gangsters e génios do crime insanos de Gotham City. Com uma impressionante galeria de vilões – incluindo alguns dos criminosos mais perigosos de Gotham City, como Catwoman, Joker, Enigma, Duas Caras, Harley Quinn, Pinguim, Mister Freeze e muitos outros – o jogo vai fazer-te entrar na pele do Cavaleiro das Trevas e impor a justiça nas ruas de Gotham City.

Batman: Arkham City – Game of The Year Edition inclui os seguintes DLC:

  • Pacote – Catwoman

  • Conjunto – Asa Noturna

  • Conjunto – Robin

  • Vingança de Harley Quinn

  • Pacote de Challenge Maps

  • Pacote de Visuais de Arkham City

Batman: Arkham City – Game of The Year Edition inclui novos conteúdos jogáveis, sete mapas, três personagens jogáveis e 12 visuais extra em relação à versão original:

  • Mapas: Wayne Manor, Main Hall, Freight Train, Black Mask, The Joker's Carnival, Iceberg Lounge e Batcave

  • Personagens jogáveis: Catwoman, Robin e Asa Noturna

  • Visuais: 1970s Batsuit, Year One Batman, The Dark Knight Returns, Earth One Batman, Batman Beyond Batman, Animated Batman, Sinestro Corps Batman, Long Halloween Catwoman, Animated Catwoman, Animated Robin, Red Robin e Animated Nightwing

  • * All Mac minis released since Late 2012
  • * All iMacs released since Late 2012
  • * All iMac Pro released since Late 2017

Pre 10.14 Users:

Players using a version of OS X before 10.14 can access a compatible version of the game via the Beta tab in the game’s properties window. Select the ‘mac_retail_11 - macOS 10.13.6 or older only' branch for a version that is compatible with 10.9.5 up to 10.13.6.

reviews.review:
After playing [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/1817070/Marvels_SpiderMan_Remastered/]Marvel's Spider-Man[/url], I decided to replay this game, and it's amazing how Arkham City did such a better job being a superhero game, despite being made like 7 years earlier. The main thing that Arkham City does better is that, besides having good main story missions, the side missions [i]actually matter,[/i] and introduce you to various villains and allies. It's rare that I play a game with side missions and they don't feel like a bit of a chore, but for each side mission in Arkham City I really want to do it because I know it will be a fun and satisfying experience. If you want to know more about where Arkham City succeeds and modern superhero games may fail, you might want to check out [url=https://steamcommunity.com/id/saltyjuniper/recommended/1817070/]my review for Marvel's Spider-Man[/url] where I wrote more of a comparison.

I don't think it's really fair to call this game "Open World", at least by modern standards, as Arkham City's overworld is quite small. However, that small overworld is packed full of content like Riddler challenges and thugs to beat up. There is a clever trick to make the world feel much larger than it is, though. One portion of the map is the Restricted Zone, which you're forced to go around, giving the accessible map a curved shape. This gives the illusion that the map is larger, since you can't go in a straight line to get from Joker's hideout at one end to Penguin's hideout at the other. There's no fast travel, but since the map is relatively small and traversal is fast and fun, there's no need for it.

Combat feels methodical and fun, and you usually have several choices for how you're going to handle a crowd of enemies. Will you disassemble an enemy's gun so nobody else can use it, or electrocute him so he shoots wildly and scares the rest of the enemies? Will you yank a distant enemy with the grappling gun to bring him closer, or knock him down with a batarang?

I wasn't too fond of the bosses overall, but I did like the [spoiler]Ra's al Ghul[/spoiler] fight and the [spoiler]Mr. Freeze[/spoiler] fight. Ironically the best part of the [spoiler]Ra's al Ghul[/spoiler] fight is actually when you're not fighting him, but a huge crowd of enemies, and it's a good test of your endurance and mastery of the game's fighting style. [spoiler]Mr. Freeze[/spoiler] is a stealth challenge, and might honestly be the best stealth-based boss fight in gaming history, putting you in a room filled with tactics you can use, but each time you the enemy adapts so you can't try the same trick twice.

And of course being able to play as Catwoman is fun. It's a bit ironic that I think Batman actually moves faster in combat (his ground takedown and counter animations feel faster), considering Catwoman is supposed to be the agile one, but overall her style is both unique enough and deep enough to be worth playing, although Batman has more options for both stealth and combat.

The story itself is peak Batman. I like that it's not just a mission to save innocent people, but also to save criminals from cruel and unusual punishment in this prison city, as it highlights that Batman is also about giving criminals a chance to reform (even if they never actually do). It is odd, though, that from the beginning the villain Hugo Strange knows that Batman is Bruce Wayne, but this has almost no importance to the story. I guess maybe Dr. Strange wants to be able to beat Batman without revealing his identity, but it just doesn't feel like Batman's identity being known is as big of an issue as it should be.

If I had any complaint, it's that there's too many Riddler challenges. When you're just progressing through the game they make a fun diversion, and it's nice that each challenge is a unique puzzle. But with so many, you're almost guaranteed to complete the game before you find them all, so you'll reach a point where Riddler challenges are the [i]only[/i] thing you're doing for a while. And Riddler's actual side quest requires you to complete these challenges to get access to his actual challenge rooms where you can save his hostages.

Regarding the quality of the PC version, the only issue I had is that somehow playing this game makes Windows think my Bluetooth headphones are speakers, and the first time I booted this game up Windows decided to crank my volume all the way up to 100 and destroy my eardrums.
